summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of recurrent acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening lower extremity pain, erythema, and swelling. He had recently missed doses of ruxolitinib, likely triggering a GVHD flare. Blood cultures revealed pseudomonas bacteremia, likely originating from chronically colonized leg wounds. He developed sepsis, acute hypoxic respiratory failure, and hospital-acquired pneumonia, requiring ICU admission, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and respiratory support with BiPAP and high-flow oxygen. His heart failure worsened with volume overload, necessitating aggressive diuresis. A new T4 compression fracture was identified, consistent with steroid-induced osteoporosis. Infectious disease guided antibiotic narrowing to ciprofloxacin, and his condition gradually improved over 24 days. He was discharged to extended care on IV ciprofloxacin, prednisone, ruxolitinib, and other baseline medications with plans for outpatient follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Other osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
